sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition has been filed, under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short, 'Cr.P.C.'), by the petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 5, who are parents, sister and brother-in-law of accused No.1, seeking to quash the proceedings against them in C.C.No.9141 of 2022 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Mahila Court,
Hyderabad, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 406 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2.

sentences.text: The brief history of the case is that one Mrs.Syeda Nida Masarath has lodged a report before the police on 31.05.2022 stating that her marriage was performed with one Mr.Syed Yaseen Nihal (accused No.1) on 22.02.2022 at Mysore and at the time of marriage, on demand, her parents gave a sum of Rs.23,00,000/- cash, 30 tulas of gold and house-hold articles, worth Rs.25,00,000/- to accused No.1 towards dowry.
Her parents have spent Rs.5,00,000/- towards marriage expenses.
Immediately, after the marriage accused No.1 and his parents demanded the de facto complainant for additional dowry of Rs.50,00,000/- for purchasing the plot at Hyderabad.
Accused No.1 used to suspect her fidelity and pressurize her to visit the Gynaecologist to confirm her virginity.
Accused No.1 used to give sleeping pills to her stating that she is mentally unstable.
But, accused No.1 is suffering from mental ill-health and he forced her to tie her hands and legs to perform sexual acts.

While the things stood thus, on 27.03.2022 the de facto complainant, accused No1, petitioner No.2-mother-in-law and others visited her cousin's house at Nizamabad wherein petitioner No.2-mother-in- law told that she had given one Crore rupees to her son-in-law thereby he became Surgeon and on that pretext, she demanded the parents of the de facto complainant to give additional dowry of Rs.50,00,000/- to start business by accused No.1 at Qatar.

By showing one or the other reason, accused No.1 and his family used to threaten her to give divorce and that they also used to abuse the de facto complainant and her parents in unparliamentary language.

Further,
petitioner No.3 used to advise the de facto complainant to give divorce to accused No.1 and search for another man as accused No.1 is very arrogant and rude.
The de facto complainant bear all the ill-treatment meted out by her in the hands of the accused with a fond hope that they would mend their behaviour towards her, but it was in vain.
As there was no other go and owing to her inability to fulfil the demands of the accused, she took shelter at the house of maternal uncle at Mehdipatnam.
With the acts of the accused, the de facto complainant has undergone mental trauma and agony.

3. sentences.text: The petitioners are innocent and they did not commit any offence as alleged by the de facto complainant.
Even accepted the allegations made in the complaint in toto, there are no reasonable grounds to believe that the petitioners are guilty for the allegations made against them.

Though they have never interfered with the family affairs of accused No.1 and the de facto complainant, knowing fully that they have nothing to do with the present case, only on vague and omnibus allegations, they have been lugged in the crime only to harass them adopting this method to dominate in her matrimonial home.
The registration, investigation thereof and continuation of further proceedings are all illegal and abuse of process of law.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance on State of Harayana v. Bhajan Lal 1 and Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam v. State of Bihar 2.
4.

sentences.text: Heard Mr.G.Ravi Mohan, learned Senior Counsel representing Mr.G.Naresh Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr.C.Sharan Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the record.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that after the marriage the de facto complainant and accused No.1 went to the house of her parents and accused No.1 stayed upto 13.04.2022 in the house of her parents, later, he went to Qatar and that there is no occasion to them to stay with the de facto complainant.
Whereas, the de facto complainant alleged that on 13.04.2022 she went to Mysore to join her husband but at that point of time, accused No.1 went to Qatar.
Except vague and omnibus allegations, there are no specific allegations against the petitioners.
Therefore, prays this Court to quash the proceedings against the petitioners.

AIR 1992 SC 604 (2022) 6 Supreme Court Cases 599.
6.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that there are clear allegations against all the petitioners, especially, petitioner No.2-mother-in-law insisted the de facto complainant to go for second marriage as her son was adamant in nature and he did not change his behaviour and that she also abused the de facto complainant and her family members in filthy language.
Therefore, it requires full-fledged trial and sought for dismissal of the petition.

7. As could be seen from the material available on record, it unfolds that the petitioners are the family members of the husband of the de facto complainant i.e., in-laws, sister-in-law and husband of the sister-in-law and that the allegations made against these petitioners are that they all used to abuse her and torture her.

The investigation done by the police reveals that right from the date of marriage, accused Nos.1 and 3 have demanded the de facto complainant to bring additional dowry from the house of her parents and that accused No.1 used to suspect her fidelity and asked her to visit the Gynaecologist to confirm her virginity and that he used to force her for sexual intercourse by tying her hands and legs.
8.

In Kahkashan Kausar (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to observe as follows:
"...17.

The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the Syed Nayeemulla And 3 Others vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102587909/

sentences.text:
increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.

20. Here it must be borne in mind that although the two FIRs may constitute two independent instances, based on separate transactions, the present complaint fails to establish specific allegations against the in-laws of the Respondent wife.
Allowing prosecution in the absence of clear allegations against the in-laws Appellants would simply result in an abuse of the process of law.

21. Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the accused appellants, it would be unjust if the Appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this court in varied instances, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged...."

9. On the face of the record, there are no specific allegations made out against petitioner Nos.1, 3 and 4 by the de facto complainant either in the complaint lodged before the police or in her detailed statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.

However, when coming to the case of petitioner No.2-mother-in- law, the de facto complainant has alleged that her mother-in-law used to abuse her and her family members in unparliamentary language and she made demands for want of additional dowry for starting business by her son (accused No.1) in Qatar and also for purchasing plot in Hyderabad and that she told her to leave his son and search for another man.
The allegations levelled against petitioner No.2 make out prima facie case and the truth or otherwise would be made out only after full-fledged trial.

10. By relying on the above referred legal proposition and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Criminal Petition is liable to be allowed as against petitioner Nos.1, 3 and 4 and the Criminal Petition is dismissed against petitioner No.2/accused No.3.
11.

In the result, this Criminal Petition is allowed partly, quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.9141 of 2022 on the file of the XIII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Nampally, Mahila Court,
Hyderabad, against petitioner Nos.1, 3 and 4/accused Nos.2, 4 and 5.
